I farm in Quzhou County, so I will keep to the cropping pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is what fits my land, my water conditions, and the local weather best. At the start of the growing season, my wheat is already in the field from autumn sowing, so my first job is to manage that crop carefully through spring with topdressing, watering when needed, and pest control only when I see pressure. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize right away so I do not lose soil moisture or growing time. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is steady and familiar, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is better and the plants are stronger. I will not spread myself across too many crops, because I want work that I can finish on time with the labor and money I have. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive amounts, because I need stable yield and controlled costs. I will do rotary tillage because it is practical and suits the machinery I would use. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield, but to get a reliable harvest from both seasons on the same land.
